title: PARTROOT196-E28: exact 2/sqrt3 sieve with the byte-maximal 28-step ladder envelope (clean input)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration specified in full in proof.md and virtual.md of this snapshot (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies (virtual.md 13). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, its total charged sequential work satisfies T = O(E(n)) by the explicit common bound C*2^((2/sqrt3) sqrt n + 512 n^(7/16)) proved in virtual.md 15.1 and proof.md 8-10, and the absorption Lemma E.3 with E.4 of envelope.md, with E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - M sum_{i=1..27} n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M+1-i)) - M2 n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M-27))), where M = 10^256 - 1, M2 is DEFINED as the positive integer whose decimal digits are the coefficient of the last structured exponent term without its minus sign (an all-nines integer with fewer digits than M, so 1 <= M2 <= M; the proof uses only this inequality, never its digit count) and a = P/Q is the exact rational of envelope.md E.1 (256-digit P and Q with 3P^2 - 4Q^2 = 3, so a > 2/sqrt3); E is exactly the structured bound (29 exponent terms: the leading term, 27 ladder terms with coefficient -M, one last ladder term with coefficient -M2; outer nPower 0 and outer logPower 0). The growth index of E is exactly 1/2 (envelope.md E.2). These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration specified in full in proof.md and virtual.md of this snapshot (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies (virtual.md 13). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, its peak allocated classical bits satisfy S_C = O(n) (proof.md 8). The envelope B_C(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration specified in full in proof.md and virtual.md of this snapshot (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies (virtual.md 13). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, its peak allocated qubits, including the fully initialized bank prefix, unknown pool and source register, satisfy S_Q = O(E(n)) by the explicit common bound C*2^((2/sqrt3) sqrt n + 512 n^(7/16)) proved in virtual.md 15.1 and proof.md 8-10, and the absorption Lemma E.3 with E.4 of envelope.md, with the same E(n) as the time claim: E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - M sum_{i=1..27} n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M+1-i)) - M2 n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M-27))), where M = 10^256 - 1, M2 is DEFINED as the positive integer whose decimal digits are the coefficient of the last structured exponent term without its minus sign (an all-nines integer with fewer digits than M, so 1 <= M2 <= M; the proof uses only this inequality, never its digit count) and a = P/Q is the exact rational of envelope.md E.1 (256-digit P and Q with 3P^2 - 4Q^2 = 3, so a > 2/sqrt3); E is exactly the structured bound (29 exponent terms: the leading term, 27 ladder terms with coefficient -M, one last ladder term with coefficient -M2; outer nPower 0 and outer logPower 0). The growth index of E is exactly 1/2. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single PARTROOT196 algorithm and configuration specified in full in proof.md and virtual.md of this snapshot (finite streaming tester with n+10 shifted X-tests per candidate for n < 2^512; for n >= 2^512, z0 = min{j: 3j^2 >= n}, z = z0 + 16 ceil(log2 n), ell = m = dl = z, growing odd-partition k = least odd >= ceil(n^(1/8)), rolling backward C_i, Y = ceil(log2 C0), u = max(Y, 2z) + 2, Qcap = 4nC0 + K, and the fully counted physical bank of proof.md) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-7 from independent ideal copies (virtual.md 13). On EVERY execution branch, including every failure, discard, retry, partial attempt and abort, the total number Q of fresh source copies acquired, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, satisfies Q = O(E(n)) by the explicit common bound C*2^((2/sqrt3) sqrt n + 512 n^(7/16)) proved in virtual.md 15.1 and proof.md 8-10, and the absorption Lemma E.3 with E.4 of envelope.md, with the same E(n): E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - M sum_{i=1..27} n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M+1-i)) - M2 n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(M-27))), where M = 10^256 - 1, M2 is DEFINED as the positive integer whose decimal digits are the coefficient of the last structured exponent term without its minus sign (an all-nines integer with fewer digits than M, so 1 <= M2 <= M; the proof uses only this inequality, never its digit count) and a = P/Q is the exact rational of envelope.md E.1 (256-digit P and Q with 3P^2 - 4Q^2 = 3, so a > 2/sqrt3); E is exactly the structured bound (29 exponent terms: the leading term, 27 ladder terms with coefficient -M, one last ladder term with coefficient -M2; outer nPower 0 and outer logPower 0). The growth index of E is exactly 1/2. These four resource bounds hold jointly for this one algorithm and configuration, together with the tolerance claim.

For the same algorithm and configuration, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q acquired copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and s, the algorithm recovers the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-7 > 2/3 jointly with the four resource bounds above (virtual.md 13, envelope.md E.4). No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
